sourcedFrom: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet (undated — no copyright line is printed)
cleanIntro: Taylor's sells this gun with Uberti's black powder revolver leaflet, a category manual that covers its guns by pattern rather than by name and publishes two different strips. This is the Colt-pattern one: wedge out, barrel forward, cylinder off the pin. Black powder fouling is corrosive, so this is a clean you do the same day you shoot.

steps.title: Unloaded confirmed and every nipple checked for a cap
steps.action: Treat it as loaded, then prove otherwise. Set the hammer at half cock so the cylinder turns, and walk every nipple round looking for percussion caps — fired ones and unfired ones both. Pull any cap you find straight away. A cap left on a nipple is a live primer sitting on a chamber you are about to take apart.
steps.caution: Place hammer in the half-cock position.
steps.quote: Rotate the cylinder to see that all the nipples are void of percussion caps. Remove any percussion caps immediately.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — LOADING AND SHOOTING, item 4, p.1 (single-page leaflet, no printed folio)

steps.title: A cylinder off the gun can still fire
steps.action: If the cylinder still has a loaded chamber in it, every cap must come off the nipples before the cylinder leaves the frame — a capped chamber will fire sitting on the bench, with nothing containing it. Uberti says so directly. Check the nipples again rather than assuming the last step got them all.
steps.quote: Note: If cylinder with loaded chamber must be removed, be sure all (unfired and fired) caps have been removed from the nipples. It is possible for a chamber to fire even though not in the gun. This could cause serious damage to the shooter.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — MALFUNCTIONS, note following item 6, p.1
steps.warn: Treat a misfire or failure to fire as though the revolver can fire at any time.

steps.title: Which pattern you have — this leaflet publishes two strips
steps.action: The leaflet covers Uberti's whole black powder range by pattern and names no individual gun, so it prints two disassemblies and expects you to know which is yours. Look just forward of the cylinder: a flat wedge driven crossways through the barrel lug means the Colt open-top pattern, which is the strip that follows. The other procedure is for a solid-framed Remington-pattern revolver with a T-shaped cylinder pin and no wedge — if your gun has no wedge, stop here, because none of the following steps fits it.
steps.aside: Disassembly of the Colt-style revolver (see fig. 1):
steps.quote: All Colt- and Remington-style revolvers are provided with intermediate pins or slots between the single chambers on the rear face of cylinder.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — LOADING AND SHOOTING, note following item 16, p.1

steps.title: Wedge tapped through from the right
steps.action: Drive the wedge out of its slot from the RIGHT side of the barrel, so it travels out to the left. It is a taper, so it only comes out the one way — going at it from the wrong side just sets it tighter. Tap it rather than levering it.
steps.quote: Remove the wedge, located just forward of the cylinder, by tapping it through the slot from the right side of the barrel.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — PREPARATION BEFORE LOADING, item 2a, p.1

steps.title: Hammer to the first audible click
steps.action: Put the hammer at half cock — Uberti describes it as the first audible click. That frees the cylinder to turn, which the next step needs. If the cylinder still will not rotate you have gone past half cock or not reached it.
steps.quote: Place the hammer in the half-cock position (first audible “click”).
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — PREPARATION BEFORE LOADING, item 2b, p.1

steps.title: Cylinder indexed so the rammer lands between chambers
steps.action: Turn the cylinder until the loading lever, when you drop it, will come down on the solid metal between two chambers rather than into a chamber mouth. Then use the lever against that spot to help move the barrel forward off the cylinder pin. Get the indexing wrong and the rammer goes into a chamber instead, which achieves nothing and can mark the chamber mouth.
steps.aside: This allows the loading lever to help in removal of the barrel from the frame and cylinder pin.
steps.quote: Rotate the cylinder, so that the loading lever, when lowered, will hit the area between the cylinder chambers.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — PREPARATION BEFORE LOADING, item 2c, p.1

steps.title: Cylinder off the pin
steps.action: With the barrel off, the cylinder comes off the cylinder pin. Support it as it comes so it does not land on its nipples. Keep the pin's grooves in mind: they take grease on the way back together, and that is what keeps the cylinder turning freely as fouling builds.
steps.quote: Remove the cylinder from the frame.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — PREPARATION BEFORE LOADING, item 2d, p.1

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Barrel, cylinder and frame are separate and that is the strip this leaflet publishes. Everything from here is cleaning, and with black powder it cannot wait — the fouling is corrosive and starts working immediately. The book's full clean is a complete strip and a hot-water wash, described in the checklist.
steps.quote: Black powder fouling is extremely corrosive and can rust the barrel and cylinder in a short time. All black powder guns must be thoroughly cleaned after firing is completed.
steps.cite: Uberti Black Powder Revolvers Instruction Manual — undated — no edition code, revision or date is printed anywhere on the leaflet — CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE, item 1, p.1
steps.warn: Warning: Use of smokeless powder in any muzzleloader revolver will result in excessively high presure and can cause serious damage to the firearm and possibly to the shooter.

deepAbsentReason: The leaflet's own deeper procedure is the CLEANING AND MAINTENANCE sequence — completely disassemble, wipe the grips, hot water and detergent or black powder solvent, boiling rinse, dry, rust preventative, oil and grease the cylinder pin grooves — and it is carried in the cleaning checklist rather than as walked steps, because the document gives it as a seven-item wash routine and not as a parts teardown. This is a category manual that names no model, so nothing model-specific has been inferred from it. The leaflet's nipple work (nipple wrench, nipple pick, removing a nipple to clear a charge) appears only inside the MALFUNCTIONS drill for a misfire, not as a maintenance procedure, so it is not presented here as a cleaning step. The one procedure the document attaches to this pattern is the four-part strip above.

cleaning.name: CHAMBERS & BARREL
tasks: Swab the inside of every chamber with a cotton swab dipped in cleaning solvent
Stand the cylinder chambers-down so the solvent drains out instead of sitting in the chambers
Run a solvent-soaked patch through the barrel, then clean dry swabs and patches through both chambers and barrel

cleaning.name: FULL WASH AFTER FIRING
tasks: Take the gun completely apart and wipe the grips off
Soak the metal parts in hot water and dish detergent and wipe the fouling away, or scrub it off with a brush and black powder solvent
Rinse everything in boiling hot water and dry it thoroughly

cleaning.name: PROTECT & LUBRICATE
tasks: Once cool, wipe every part with a rust preventative
Lightly oil the moving parts and grease the grooves of the cylinder pin
Store it somewhere dry with enough ventilation

reassembly: Grease the cylinder pin grooves, then put the cylinder back onto the pin.
Bring the barrel back over the pin and onto the frame.
Tap the wedge back into its slot from the left so it seats the way it came out.
Oil all moving parts lightly on the way back together — heavy oil just collects fouling.
If you are shooting again the same day, leave the inside of the chambers and the nipples dry.
fncheck: With the revolver confirmed empty and uncapped, check the wedge is seated and the barrel is firm on the frame. Bring the hammer to half cock and confirm the cylinder rotates freely with no drag from a dry or fouled pin, then confirm it locks up as the hammer comes to full cock. Confirm the loading lever latches back up under the barrel rather than hanging loose, and confirm the hammer will sit on a pin or slot between chambers, which is the leaflet's own carry position.
